prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No robot lets older people live at home in dignity at scale, so the Main KPI of 300,000,000 older people with robotic care is unmet. The controlled evidence is for social companion robots, mostly in institutions: a meta-analysis of 8 RCTs found large effects of social robots on depression and loneliness among long-term-care residents (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jamda.2024.02.017), a 2025 integrative review covers care robots for community-dwelling older adults (https://doi.org/10.4258/hir.2025.31.4.347), and staff studies document service-robot experiences in aged care (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-86255-w). Physical home care is not solved: a 2026 Japanese lottery-based natural experiment studies care-robot adoption in long-term care facilities, not homes (https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9001048/v1), and the leading home humanoid, 1X NEO, relied on remote teleoperators and was not confirmed delivered by August 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1X_Technologies). GitHub eldercare-robot repositories are student ROS projects. Honest limit: companion robots and fall-detection sensors are known answers and tasks that redeploy them are not new work; the open, checkable work is safe physical assistance at home, such as transfers, toileting support and fall response, validated with older adults.
